title: Paul's Speech Through Stoic Ears
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Mediterranean Travels
description: Ten lines paraphrased from Paul's Areopagus speech (Acts 17:22-31) in speech order; the learner predicts whether a Stoic listener would hear each as common ground or something new, sees each line placed on a strip with its Stoic background, and then reads the audience's reaction from Acts 17:32-34.

educational.topic: Paul's Areopagus speech and the Stoic and Epicurean ideas it echoes
learningObjectives: Differentiate the lines of Paul's Areopagus speech that build on what Stoic listeners already believed from the lines that ask them to accept something new, judging at least 8 of 10 lines correctly on the first attempt.
prerequisites: The Areopagus speech and its five moves

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Predict, then reveal, line by line, with each line placed on a two-lane strip and a final reveal of the audience's reaction
keyQuestions: Would a Stoic listener already agree with this line, or is it something new?
Where in the speech does it turn from common ground to new claims?
At what point does Acts say the audience scoffed?
commonMisconceptions: Paul dropped his own message to please philosophers.
Every idea in the speech was new to Greeks.
'We are his offspring' comes from the Hebrew Bible, rather than from the poet Aratus.
The Athenians rejected the speech as a whole, when Acts says they reacted at the resurrection.
assessmentOpportunities: First-attempt predictions on ten lines (mastery: 8 of 10, with lines 9 and 10 correct).
Explain why quoting Aratus would persuade this audience.
